update_cadence: Historical. Changes only if a source correction is found; regenerate with scripts/build-historical.py.

series.label: US unemployment rate, annual (1929-1947)
series.source: US Census Bureau, Historical Statistics of the United States, Colonial Times to 1970, Series D85-86, p.135
series.note: Annual averages, persons 14 and over (16 and over for 1947). 1929-1939 are Lebergott's reconstructions as published by the Census Bureau; the CPS household survey begins in 1940. Relief workers on federal emergency programmes count as unemployed here; see disputed.

splices.note: The CPS household survey begins March 1940; earlier years are census-benchmark reconstructions.

disputed.note: Whether a WPA relief job was a job. Counting federal emergency relief workers as employed, Darby (1976) puts 1933 at 20.6% against the 24.9% shown, and 1941 at 6.6% against 9.9%. The gap is definitional, not arithmetic, and it is the difference between 'a quarter of the labour force idle' and 'a fifth'.
disputed.source: Michael Darby, 'Three-and-a-half million U.S. employees have been mislaid', Journal of Political Economy 84(1), 1976

series.label: Canada unemployment rate, June (1921-1945)
series.source: Statistics Canada, Historical Statistics of Canada (11-516-X), Series D124-133; rate derived as persons without jobs and seeking work over the civilian labour force
series.note: 1 June of each year, persons 14 and over, excludes Newfoundland (joined Confederation in 1949). Census benchmarks (1921, 1931, 1941) extrapolated between censuses with trade-union and employer reports; the Dominion Bureau of Statistics' own reconstruction, and the best available measure of the period. June readings run slightly below annual averages.

series.label: Canada unemployment rate, annual (1946-1975)
series.source: Statistics Canada, Historical Statistics of Canada (11-516-X), Series D223-235 (total, series D233)
series.note: Labour Force Survey annual averages on the original 14-and-over basis (the survey ran quarterly 1946-1952, monthly after). The post-1976 revised 15-and-over basis reads one to three tenths lower where the two overlap; the monthly series on this page begins in 1976 on the current basis.

splices.note: LFS moves from quarterly to monthly collection; annual averages either side.
